text: Israel has launched a major project to channel desalinated Mediterranean seawater into the Sea of Galilee after years of drought pushed the lake’s levels dangerously close to the “black line,” where pumping risks permanent ecological damage. Water from coastal plants in Ashdod, Hadera, and other sites will be rerouted through upgraded pumping stations, new pipelines, and reinforced reservoirs. In the coming weeks, the system will pump about 5,000 cubic meters (1.3 million gallons) per hour, with long-term plans to triple that capacity. The 1-billion-shekel ($297 million) initiative aims not only to secure Israel’s water supply but also to revive local ecosystems, including the once-dry Zalmon stream.
